title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 19 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 19 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 19 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 19.

questions.question: Who met Jehoshaphat as he returned to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him as stated in 2 Chronicles 19:2.

questions.question: What was said to be upon Jehoshaphat because he helped the ungodly?
questions.explanation: The verse states that wrath is upon him from before the LORD, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 19:2.

questions.question: What good things were found in Jehoshaphat?
questions.explanation: The text mentions that he took away the groves out of the land, which is noted in 2 Chronicles 19:3.

questions.question: Where did Jehoshaphat go to bring the people back to the Lord?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat went out from Beersheba to mount Ephraim to bring the people back unto the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 19:4.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat returned to Jerusalem in peace.
questions.explanation: The chapter begins by stating that Jehoshaphat returned to his house in peace to Jerusalem, as seen in 2 Chronicles 19:1.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat set throughout all the fenced cities of Judah?
questions.explanation: He set judges in the land throughout all the fenced cities of Judah, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 19:5.

questions.question: True or False: The judges were told to judge for man.
questions.explanation: The judges were instructed not to judge for man, but for the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 19:6.

questions.question: What were the judges warned against in their judgments?
questions.explanation: Judges were warned that there is no iniquity with the LORD our God, as stated in 2 Chronicles 19:7.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat charged the Levites to act with a perfect heart.
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat charged the Levites to do so in the fear of the LORD, faithfully, and with a perfect heart, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 19:9.

questions.question: Who is mentioned as the chief priest overseeing matters of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Amariah the chief priest is mentioned as being over all matters of the LORD in 2 Chronicles 19:11.

questions.question: What should the judges do if they find a cause among their brethren?
questions.explanation: They were instructed to warn them that they trespass not against the LORD, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 19:10.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat was criticized for his actions by Jehu.
questions.explanation: Jehu criticized Jehoshaphat for helping the ungodly and loving those who hate the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 19:2.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 19 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 19 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What action did Jehoshaphat take throughout Judah after returning to Jerusalem?
options: He set judges in the land
questions.correctAnswer: He set judges in the land
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat set judges in the land throughout all the fenced cities of Judah, city by city, as stated in 2 Chronicles 19:5.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 19:6, who do the judges ultimately judge for?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that the judges are instructed to take heed because they judge not for man, but for the LORD, who is with them in the judgment (2 Chronicles 19:6).

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 19:7 warn against in the judgment process?
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that there is no iniquity with the LORD our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts (2 Chronicles 19:7).

questions.question: Who was responsible for spiritual matters in Jerusalem according to 2 Chronicles 19:11?
questions.explanation: Amariah the chief priest was over all matters of the LORD as stated in 2 Chronicles 19:11.

questions.question: What does Jehoshaphat encourage his judges to do in 2 Chronicles 19:9?
options: Do it in the fear of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Do it in the fear of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat charged them to act in the fear of the LORD, faithfully, and with a perfect heart (2 Chronicles 19:9).

questions.question: What consequence is mentioned in 2 Chronicles 19:10 for those who trespass against the LORD?
options: They will be judged by the king
questions.explanation: The verse warns that if they trespass against the LORD, wrath will come upon them and their brethren (2 Chronicles 19:10).

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat's reforms included removing groves from the land.
questions.explanation: Good things were found in Jehoshaphat because he had taken away the groves out of the land (2 Chronicles 19:3).

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat was warned to help the ungodly.
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat was warned against helping the ungodly and loving those who hate the LORD, which brought wrath upon him (2 Chronicles 19:2).

questions.question: What does Jehoshaphat emphasize to the judges in terms of their integrity?
questions.explanation: He emphasizes that they should fear the LORD and act justly, as there is no iniquity or favoritism with God (2 Chronicles 19:7).

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 19:8 describe the roles of the Levites and priests?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat set the Levites, priests, and chief fathers as officers before the people for the judgment of the LORD (2 Chronicles 19:8).

questions.question: What is the key theme of judgment as presented in 2 Chronicles 19:6-7?
options: Judgment is only for the wealthy
Judgment is based on fear of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment is based on fear of the LORD
questions.explanation: The judges are instructed to judge in the fear of the LORD, indicating that true judgment is rooted in reverence for God (2 Chronicles 19:6-7).

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat returned to Jerusalem in turmoil.
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat returned to his house in peace to Jerusalem, as stated in 2 Chronicles 19:1.

questions.question: What does Jehoshaphat's actions teach us about leadership and integrity in 2 Chronicles 19?
options: Leaders should fear God and act justly
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders should fear God and act justly
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat's emphasis on fearing the LORD and acting judiciously illustrates that leaders should prioritize integrity and accountability (2 Chronicles 19:6-7).

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 19 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 19.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat do upon returning to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat returned to his house in peace to Jerusalem as stated in 2 Chronicles 19:1.

questions.question: Who met Jehoshaphat upon his return to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him as recorded in 2 Chronicles 19:2.

questions.question: According to Jehu, what was upon Jehoshaphat because he helped the ungodly?
questions.explanation: Jehu stated that there is wrath upon Jehoshaphat from before the LORD for helping the ungodly, as noted in 2 Chronicles 19:2.

questions.question: What good things were found in Jehoshaphat according to the seer?
questions.explanation: The seer noted that Jehoshaphat had taken away the groves out of the land, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 19:3.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat do to bring the people back to God?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat went out again through the people to bring them back unto the LORD God, as stated in 2 Chronicles 19:4.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat instruct the judges to remember?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat instructed the judges that they judge not for man, but for the LORD, who is with them in judgment, as found in 2 Chronicles 19:6.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat say should be upon the judges as they judge?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat emphasized that the fear of the LORD should be upon them as they judge, as stated in 2 Chronicles 19:7.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat charge the judges to do?
questions.explanation: He charged them to do so in the fear of the LORD, faithfully, and with a perfect heart, as noted in 2 Chronicles 19:9.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 19:10, what should judges warn their brethren about?
questions.explanation: Judges were instructed to warn them not to trespass against the LORD to avoid wrath, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 19:10.

questions.question: Who is identified as the chief priest over matters of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Amariah is identified as the chief priest over all matters of the LORD in 2 Chronicles 19:11.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat dealt with his judges courageously, according to the chapter.
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat encouraged courage in dealing with judgments, as he told them to deal courageously, found in 2 Chronicles 19:11.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat only set judges in the capital city of Judah.
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat set judges throughout all the fenced cities of Judah, not just in the capital, as stated in 2 Chronicles 19:5.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of judging with righteousness found in this chapter?
questions.explanation: John 7:24 emphasizes judging not by appearance but with righteous judgment, echoing the theme found in 2 Chronicles 19:6.

questions.question: What Hebrew word in 2 Chronicles 19:10 refers to 'trespass' and implies sinning against God?
questions.explanation: 'Chata' refers to 'trespass,' implying sin against God, as seen in the context of warning against wrongdoing in 2 Chronicles 19:10.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Jehoshaphat's charge to the judges, emphasizing the importance of their role?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat's instruction to judge faithfully and in the fear of the LORD demonstrates parallelism, stressing the dual importance of their actions in 2 Chronicles 19:9.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 19 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 19 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What was the consequence of Jehoshaphat's alliance with the ungodly according to the prophet Jehu?
options: He faced wrath from the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He faced wrath from the LORD
questions.explanation: Jehu warns Jehoshaphat that his alliance with the ungodly has brought wrath upon him from the LORD (2 Chronicles 19:2).

questions.question: Which action did Jehoshaphat take that was seen as good in the eyes of the LORD?
questions.explanation: The prophet Jehu acknowledges that Jehoshaphat has done good by removing the groves from the land (2 Chronicles 19:3).

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat do after returning to Jerusalem from peace?
options: Brought the people back to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Brought the people back to the LORD
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat went out among the people to bring them back to the LORD God of their fathers (2 Chronicles 19:4).

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat instruct the judges regarding their judgments?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat instructed the judges that they do not judge for man but for the LORD, who is with them in judgment (2 Chronicles 19:6).

questions.question: According to Jehoshaphat, what should the judges have upon them?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat called for the fear of the LORD to be upon the judges as they carry out their duties (2 Chronicles 19:7).

questions.question: What was the role of Amariah in Jehoshaphat's administration?
options: Chief priest over matters of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Chief priest over matters of the LORD
questions.explanation: Amariah was designated as the chief priest over all matters of the LORD (2 Chronicles 19:11).

questions.question: What is emphasized about God's character in relation to judgment?
questions.explanation: The text emphasizes that there is no iniquity with the LORD our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts (2 Chronicles 19:7).

questions.question: What specific responsibility did Jehoshaphat give to the Levites and priests?
options: For the judgment of the LORD and controversies
To train the people in warfare
questions.correctAnswer: For the judgment of the LORD and controversies
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat set Levites and priests for the judgment of the LORD and for resolving controversies in Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 19:8).

questions.question: What warning did Jehoshaphat give regarding matters of law and commandments?
options: To warn brethren not to trespass against the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To warn brethren not to trespass against the LORD
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat charged the judges to warn their brethren not to trespass against the LORD to avoid bringing wrath upon them (2 Chronicles 19:10).

questions.question: What doctrinal insight is provided by verses 5-6 and verse 11 regarding leadership?
questions.explanation: These verses teach that leaders must judge with the fear of the LORD because they are accountable to Him in their judgments (2 Chronicles 19:5-6, 11).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in His lack of iniquity and impartiality?
questions.explanation: God's lack of iniquity and impartiality reflects His holiness, as He is without sin and treats all equally (2 Chronicles 19:7).

questions.question: How does the chapter illustrate the importance of seeking God in leadership?
options: By preparing one's heart to seek God
By forming alliances with other nations
questions.correctAnswer: By preparing one's heart to seek God
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat's preparation of his heart to seek God is highlighted as a key aspect of his leadership (2 Chronicles 19:3).

questions.question: What does the warning against taking gifts imply about divine justice?
questions.explanation: The warning against taking gifts emphasizes that God's justice is uncorrupted, as He does not show favoritism (2 Chronicles 19:7).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not care about human justice. What does 2 Chronicles 19 teach?
options: God holds leaders accountable for justice
questions.correctAnswer: God holds leaders accountable for justice
questions.explanation: The chapter teaches that God expects leaders to judge with integrity and fear, indicating His concern for justice (2 Chronicles 19:6-7).

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 9 and 10 convey about the responsibilities of judges?
options: Judges must focus on personal gain
Judges should act in fear of the LORD and warn others against sin
questions.correctAnswer: Judges should act in fear of the LORD and warn others against sin
questions.explanation: These verses emphasize that judges must carry out their duties in the fear of the LORD and actively warn others not to sin (2 Chronicles 19:9-10).
